metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

evidence: verify command `grep -q 'REBAR_VERIFY_ENABLE_CODE_REVIEW' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md && grep -q '## Preview the review locally' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` greps the unanchored word 'REBAR_VERIFY_ENABLE_CODE_REVIEW' — it substring-matches (e.g. 'review_REBAR_VERIFY_ENABLE_CODE_REVIEW'); anchor it (\b, ^$, or a quoted key like '"REBAR_VERIFY_ENABLE_CODE_REVIEW":')

verify command `grep -q 'rebar review-code — optional local preview' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` greps the unanchored word 'rebar' — it substring-matches (e.g. 'review_rebar'); anchor it (\b, ^$, or a quoted key like '"rebar":')

verify command `grep -q 'preview the review locally with .rebar review-code' AGENTS.md` greps the unanchored word 'preview' — it substring-matches (e.g. 'review_preview'); anchor it (\b, ^$, or a quoted key like '"preview":')
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile AC1 and AC5 by aligning the grep patterns to the same heading: either update AC1 to `grep -q '## Preview the review locally before you push'` (if the heading includes 'before you push') or update AC5 to `grep -q '#preview-the-review-locally'` (if the heading is the shorter form) — and update the Scope bullet to quote the exact heading text.
evidence: AC1 proving command: `grep -q '## Preview the review locally' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`

AC5 rationale: 'GitHub-generated anchor `#preview-the-review-locally-before-you-push` matches the heading text' — GitHub slugifies heading text verbatim, so the heading must literally end in '…before you push' to produce this anchor.

If the heading is `## Preview the review locally`, GitHub generates `#preview-the-review-locally` (not `…before-you-push`), so AC5 fails. If the heading is `## Preview the review locally before you push`, AC1's substring match fails because `grep -q '## Preview the review locally'` would actually still match (substring), BUT AC1's intent is a full section-name check and the description says 'Preview the review locally' — the mismatch in the stated anchor vs stated heading creates implementation confusion regardless.
findings.finding: AC1 greps for the heading `## Preview the review locally` while AC5 checks for the GitHub-generated anchor `#preview-the-review-locally-before-you-push`, which can only be produced by a heading `## Preview the review locally before you push`. No single heading text can satisfy both greps simultaneously, making the two ACs mutually exclusive.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC1 (`grep -q '## Preview the review locally'`) and AC5 (`grep -q '#preview-the-review-locally-before-you-push'`)
scenarios: An executor writing the heading as `## Preview the review locally` satisfies AC1 but causes AC5 to fail because the anchor is wrong.

An executor writing the heading as `## Preview the review locally before you push` satisfies AC5 but the plan's prose (Scope bullet, section name quoted in AC1's description) implies a shorter heading, creating confusion about the canonical section name.
findings.suggested_fix: If the intended heading is `## Preview the review locally before you push`, update AC1's grep to `grep -q '## Preview the review locally before you push' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` and update the Scope bullet to quote that full heading. If the intended heading is the shorter form, update AC5's grep to `grep -q '#preview-the-review-locally' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` and drop 'before-you-push' from the anchor.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Anchor AC4's grep to the expected quote character by replacing `.` with the literal backtick (or whichever delimiter is intended), e.g. `grep -q 'preview the review locally with \`rebar review-code' AGENTS.md` (escaped for the shell) or use a fixed-string flag `-F` if the full literal string is known.
evidence: AC4 proving command: `grep -q 'preview the review locally with .rebar review-code' AGENTS.md`
In BRE/ERE (grep default), `.` matches any character, not a literal period or backtick — so the pattern matches any single character between 'with ' and 'rebar review-code'.
findings.finding: AC4's proving command uses `.` (unanchored regex wildcard) in place of a specific quote character, meaning `grep -q 'preview the review locally with .rebar review-code'` would match `preview the review locally withXrebar review-code` or any single-character substitution, creating a taxonomy item-1 false-positive risk.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC4 (`grep -q 'preview the review locally with .rebar review-code' AGENTS.md`)
scenarios: A line reading `preview the review locally with XREBAR_review-code` (a typo or different formatting) passes the grep even though it does not satisfy the intent of the criterion.
findings.suggested_fix: If the AGENTS.md prose uses a backtick, update AC4 to: `grep -q "preview the review locally with \`rebar review-code" AGENTS.md` or equivalently `grep -F 'preview the review locally with' AGENTS.md | grep -q 'rebar review-code'` with the specific quoting character asserted separately.
